category_specific_evidence: Issue #31608: np.asarray(pd.NaT).astype('datetime64') raises TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer; the bug is that NaT-like objects with NaN year/month/day attributes are not converted to NaT.

Patch in numpy/_core/src/multiarray/datetime.c (convert_pyobject_to_datetime) checks dts.year == NPY_DATETIME_NAT and maps NaT-like objects to NaT, bypassing unit cast-safety checks as NaT scalars do.
When meta->base is NPY_FR_ERROR (no explicit unit), the fix sets base to NPY_FR_GENERIC with num=1, which emits a DeprecationWarning about the generic unit.

Added test test_datetime_nat_like_object_conversion uses a duck-typed class with year/month/day = float('nan') and checks astype('datetime64[ns]') yields dtype M8[ns] and np.isnat, np.datetime64(obj, 'ns') is NaT, and astype('datetime64') with pytest.warns(DeprecationWarning) yields NaT.
reproduction_risks: Special value involved is NaN (NaT-like year/month/day NaN attributes); passages do not discuss +/-inf, signed zero, or subnormals.
The no-unit path emits a DeprecationWarning for the generic unit; reproduction should expect or account for this warning rather than treat it as an error.
Passages do not give numeric tolerances or magnitude regimes; the test uses exact isnat checks.
